en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Dhāraṇī of the Youth Mañjuśrī with a Single Topknot. *Namaḥ mañjuśriye kumārabhūtāya*.
*Ra-bu-da-ya tadyathā oṃ śrī-gara-be ma-hu-kha-la-be a-lam-a-bhi-ga-ra-be sa-ma-saṃ-pada-ga-ra-be svāhā.* At that time, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having spoken this dhāraṇī within the great assembly...
All Tathāgatas of the worlds in the ten directions,
along with the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings,
and the entire great assembly, all together praised him, saying:
Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta Bodhisattva Mahāsattva!
By the power of your great compassionate vow,
you act within this degenerate age out of a desire to pity and take pity upon sentient beings of meager merit.
"You have skillfully expounded this inconceivable, wish-fulfilling jewel treasury of the sublime Dharma,
which benefits sentient beings and produces inexhaustible merit and welfare.
At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the great assembly, saying:
I received this dhāraṇī from the Buddhas of the past.
Whenever beings' merit is exhausted during a kalpa of decline,
I proclaim it so that good sons and good daughters, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās in that evil age may seek the path to bodhi.
To guide all sentient beings so that they may swiftly accomplish all wholesome deeds and transcend the great ocean of suffering of birth and death,
I exhort them to receive and uphold these wondrous and sublime phrases.
If good sons or good daughters practice with diligence day and night,
constantly reciting this dhāraṇī and remembering it without forgetting,
or simply praising its inconceivable power.
Exhort others to believe and accept it,
and with a sincere heart, recite this dhāraṇī and practice deeds that bring benefit to others.
All the evil karmic offenses of these good sons and good daughters,
including all five types of immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*) accumulated since beginningless time, shall be entirely extinguished;
they shall never again sink into the great ocean of birth and death.
They shall forever be free from the fear of the three miserable realms and evil paths;
wherever they are born, they shall attain the knowledge of past lives,
their six sense organs shall be pure, and they shall be endowed with all the marks of excellence.
Possessing exquisite form, dignified and majestic, with blazing splendor,
one shall obtain all that is sought.
First, one should maintain the recitation of other mantras.
Everything shall be fully accomplished;
whatever one undertakes will be preeminent.
If one can receive and uphold this dhāraṇī, [all goals will be achieved].
All previous violations of the śīla and deficiencies in the three types of action shall become completely purified;
all karmic offenses resulting from the breaking of precepts are eliminated.
Forever free from the evil realms, they will always be born among humans and devas;
their faculties will be harmonious and supple, their wisdom pure,
and they will attain complete proficiency in all matters.
One attains the power of profound faith in the True Dharma;
whatever one says is accepted with trust by those who hear it,
and one always achieves excellence even among enemies.
All enemies shall forever cease their evil intentions and be unable to harm one another.
All devas and nāgas will constantly follow and protect them.
They will spontaneously achieve vast merit and virtue.
Those who behold me are struck with awe and submission.
Because my compassionate vows are profound and inexhaustible, and my merit and wisdom benefit all sentient beings,
I am protected and sustained by the Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the great Bodhisattvas.
Through the empowerment of the assembly of sages and by the power of their vows,
all liberations will be accomplished without exception.
I shall now further explain the ritual for receiving and upholding this dhāraṇī,
the method for painting the image, the procedure for making offerings at the maṇḍala, and the practice for seeking spiritual accomplishment.
One should first select an auspicious day according to one's vows and the positions of the planets and lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*).
The artist, having observed the eight precepts (*aṣṭāṅga-śīla*) and maintained purity,
should [paint] upon white leather or silk cloth.
Depict Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva in the form of a youth with a single topknot,
golden in color, seated in the half-lotus posture upon a thousand-petaled white lotus flower,
holding a blue lotus in his left hand.
Upon the flower is an *cintāmaṇi* jewel.
Her right hand is extended with the palm facing outward and the five fingers forming the *paripūrṇamanoratha-mudrā* (the seal of fulfilling all wishes).
She smiles joyfully.
Adorn their bodies with various pearl garlands, crowns, and necklaces;
having painted this image,
one should smear and polish a square altar in a pure room.
The positions are arranged across three courtyards from the interior outward,
enshrining seventeen deities exactly as described in the Yoga Method of the Five-Syllable Wheel.
One should offer sincere worship with exquisite, fragrant, and delicious cakes and confections.
Place this image on the eastern side of the altar,
with the practitioner facing west.
Facing the image toward the east,
one should begin the recitation on the eighth day of the waxing moon.
Each day, one should recite the aforementioned mantra eight hundred or one thousand times.
Then, lying down before the image with single-minded concentration and thinking of me, Mañjuśrī, you will fall asleep;
in your dream, you will certainly see Mañjuśrī in the form of a young boy. If you see this sign, [you shall know that you have attained success].
Know that you have already received their empowerment;
all your aspirations shall be fulfilled,
and everything you seek shall be attained.
The verbal instructions taught will be believed and accepted by all people.

Furthermore, regarding the medicinal herb called *madhūka* (this is named "white hushuai" in Chinese), once one has recited the aforementioned mantra over it eight thousand times while performing the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), [the following shall occur].
If one holds this medicine in the mouth,
then upon entering the royal palace or the residences of the hundred officials,
one's words will be answered with a response, and all that is sought shall be obtained.
One should believe, accept, and submit to the spoken teachings, not daring to oppose them.
Furthermore, regarding the medicinal substance *dīrghavaṭī*—this is called "Bodhi-bark"—one should dry it in the shade and empower it with the preceding mantra eight thousand times.
He placed [the food] in his alms bowl and went on his rounds for alms.
Whatever he required—be it food, drink, clothing, or even gold, silver, and the seven precious jewels—he obtained it all.
The multitude loved and revered him, vying with one another to present him with offerings.
One shall be victorious in all places of contention and strife.
Furthermore, on the eighth day of the waxing moon,
before this image of Mañjuśrī, one should [perform the rite].
Light a lamp and consume the three white foods.
Furthermore, offer white foods, various white flowers, and burn white sandalwood incense as an offering.
Recite this mantra eight thousand times.
Once the prescribed number of recitations was completed,
he immediately fell asleep as before. I,
Mañjuśrī, then manifested my pure and wondrous form-body before him.
All your wishes shall be fulfilled.
Every day, I will provide you with one thousand gold coins;
you must not hoard them.
In total, offer these as offerings to the Triple Gem and cultivate merit.
Recite [the mantra] eight hundred times every day,
making offerings according to one's capacity and means.
One should not allow any interruption.
Furthermore, take one silver bowl and empower it one hundred and eight times, or eight hundred times, or twenty-one times.
Place it upon a white silk cloth before an image of Mañjuśrī.
He then covered it with white silk. After one night had passed,
at dawn, he reached into the bowl with his hand and found eight hundred gold coins.
All the aforementioned practices should be performed in secret;
they must not be made known to even a single person,
with the sole exception of those who practice together and share the same aspiration for this matter.
You must have only one companion and must never speak of this to outsiders; otherwise,
the power of the empowerment will be instantly lost.
One must be cautious and discreet.
If one can act with careful diligence according to the instructions,
one will constantly provide offerings of gold and silver every day without interruption.
The aforementioned dharmas cannot all be performed together;
rather, one should accomplish a single matter according to one's own inclination.
Nevertheless, one must first discipline both body and mind.
Repeatedly drinking the five pure substances of oxen,
he gave rise to a heart of compassion and practiced with diligence day and night, never failing to follow the instructions.
One will certainly attain the realization of the supreme *siddhi* in this very life.

The Heart Mantra is: Oṃ samanaśiri hūṃ svāhā. The Anu-hṛdaya (Subsequent Heart) Mantra is: Oṃ amāni hūṃ svāhā. The Maṇḍala Boundary-binding Mantra is: Oṃ deśamani hūṃ svāhā. The Four Directions Boundary-binding Mantra is: Oṃ samantājñānamani hūṃ svāhā. With this mantra, empower water twenty-one times.

If one scatters [the offerings] in the four directions, it immediately constitutes a consecrated boundary (*sīmābandha*). If one constantly recites this mantra before the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī every day for eight hundred times without fail, [the benefit will be attained].
Every day he obtained five hundred gold coins,
which he would then offer as alms to support the Triple Gem;
he consumed only what was allotted to his own share.
One must not seek out places that lack righteous benefit or employ the practice in violation of the instructions.
One must by no means hoard or accumulate [offerings].
Rather, one should daily provide various cakes and fruits as offerings to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
When performing the ritual of extraction, do not allow it to become impure;
likewise, one’s own clothing must be extremely clean and pure.
Bathe frequently so as not to be defiled by filth.
If one sees śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas who do not follow the Dharma—
whether their complexions are haggard and withered, or their deportment is improper and their physical forms are ugly—
one must never treat them with derisive laughter or slander.
The Great Sage Mañjuśrī manifests various transformed bodies of diverse types to test and subdue the minds of those who practice,
desiring that they always give rise to compassion and maintain universal equanimity.
Toward all sentient beings, they give rise to a mind of precious respect, a mind free from discrimination,
a mind free from defiled attachment, and a mind free from excessive fondness—
vast and unimpeded.
One should maintain the thought that this will result in attaining Buddhahood in the future.
If a practitioner can abide according to these instructions, dwelling in non-conceptuality and diligently reciting the mantra,
the wishes they seek shall be swiftly fulfilled by the Great Sage Mañjuśrī.
The alms bowl will be miraculously transformed so that it is always filled to the brim, and its contents will never be exhausted even as they are used.
Furthermore, there is another method: take the root of the *chang-qi* plant and empower it eight thousand times with the aforementioned mantra, then place it within the alms bowl.
Carrying this bowl, enter the city to beg for alms;
you shall obtain whatever robes you require according to your wishes.
Furthermore, there is a method: take agallochum, white sandalwood, and storax.
These three kinds of incense are to be used for regular offerings.
In all places, one should always speak of burning this incense without interruption;
thus, whatever one seeks will be swiftly fulfilled.
Furthermore, there is a method: take five-colored thread one *jō* in length.
Recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times to empower it, then tie it into a single knot, repeating until twenty-one knots are complete.
Place the knotted thread inside the bowl and set it before the image.
Make offerings according to your means.
Mañjuśrī will appear daily within this bowl, manifesting twenty-one *liang* of the finest gold.
This gold must certainly not be kept in storage or accumulated;
it should be applied to the cultivation of merit and used for making offerings to the Triple Gem so that it is never exhausted.
If it were hidden away and accumulated, [it would serve no purpose].
It then immediately vanished and did not appear again.
Furthermore, there is a medicinal herb named *suśavarta*, also called *sasarpa*; this is translated as "white mustard seed."
Furthermore, there is a medicine named Mahāmṛta, which originates from the region of Shu.
If there is a great wind or heavy rain that falls incessantly for a long time without clearing,
one should place the two aforementioned medicines together in a single location.
Empower these two medicines eight thousand times with the Body Mantra and cast them into the air above;
the wind and rain will then immediately cease.
If at that time there is a scorching drought with no rain,
take several *śarāva* measures [of sand], empower them eight thousand times,
and scatter them into water where dragons reside.
Immediately, a great rain fell. Furthermore,
if a Dharma Master takes this empowered medicinal powder and scatters it into the midst of a great battle array,
all swords, staves, bows, and arrows will become incapable of use.
If one uses it with meditative concentration, no harm will be caused.
If it is scattered among the grass, or in the forests, or among all the crops and seedlings in the fields,
there will be no insects whatsoever capable of injuring or damaging them.
If one scatters it within a stone cave, or among bamboo groves, or in fields of non-glutinous rice and other five grains,
it will immediately multiply so that one may take from it without end.
If one scatters it upon one's own head, [the same occurs].
In all places of conflict and dispute, one shall attain excellence.
Whether entering the royal palace or the residences of great ministers and various officials,
one shall everywhere receive their commands with reverence and respect.
If one is among a group of traveling merchants or traders,
their goods shall not be subject to theft;
no bandits whatsoever will be able to plunder them.
If it is scattered in the four directions,
no ghosts, spirits, yakṣas, rākṣasas, or various malevolent demons will be able to cause harm.
If it is scattered where there is a fire, [the fire shall be extinguished].
The fire then extinguishes itself and cannot burn objects;
if it is scattered into water,
it then stops flowing and remains motionless.
Furthermore, there are many other dharmas that cannot be fully described;
it is sufficient to achieve the efficacy of the aforementioned dharmas.
Henceforth, whatever one performs according to one's own intention will be accomplished;
there is no need for exhaustive explanation,
as this is certain and beyond doubt.
This mantra possesses great majesty, radiance, and inconceivable power that is difficult to measure.
For those who achieve accomplishment through recitation, it excludes only those who lack sincere devotion.

The Sūtra on the Swift Accomplishment of the One-Braided Mañjuśrī Youth and the Inexhaustible Treasure Store. This sūtra was [translated] on the eighteenth day of the ninth month of the first year of the Shangyuan era.
The Brahmin Vajramāṇayus (in the language of Tang: *Jingang fushou*, meaning "Vajra Fortune and Longevity").

At the three courtyards of Lún Temple in Kāiyuán Monastery, Qīn Prefecture; on the third day of the third month of the seventeenth year of the Zhēnyuán era, the Sramana who translates the scriptures revisited [the site]. At the residence of Imperial Commissioner Sà of Zhōngzhōu within the Eight Gorges.
I have seen the record of the verification and inclusion in the canon by the Indian monk [Amoghavajra].

He was the former resident venerable master and guide, the teacher who led the Eight Princes—the holy ones through whom the Dharma was transmitted from the past Tathāgata Candrasūryapradīpa—and the ninth-generation patriarch of Śākyamuni Tathāgata.

In the Golden World of the East, among the four *pāramitās* within the ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata Nāga-uttama-jñāna-rāja, she is the second honored one. She is the Wisdom-Mother of the four directional Buddhas and the distinct manifestation of the same essence as the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana. Her body pervades the *dharmadhātu*, illuminating the three periods of time; she is the mother of all sages and the universal mother of all who give rise to the bodhicitta, serving as the fundamental source and the locus of reliance for attaining the fruit of realization.

The Mantra of Mañjuśrī’s Compassionate Protection: Oṃ buddhamaitrye kṣa haṃ. This may be recited when the earth is being disturbed. The Wrathful Dhāraṇī of Mañjuśrī: Oṃ vajratīkṣṇa kuru dhīna dhīna hūṃ phaṭ. Use this mantra to protect the body, expel obstacles, and establish the boundary.
Purify all incense, flowers, and all ritual implements.
May all beings universally encounter this teaching;
Mañjuśrī, you should know this.
May you swiftly realize the merit and wisdom of Prajñā, and quickly attain the state of the Unsurpassed Honored One among Two-legged Beings.

Mañjuśrī’s Incantation for Healing Wounds: *Namaḥ sarvabuddhānām acintyānubhāva-taru-piñce oṃ vṛṣa svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra for malarial fevers from the *Saptabuddha-bhaiṣajyaguru-sūtra*. *Tadyathā*: *akṣu mokṣatra kṣuma-mama-kṣu-kule ha-hu-ṅ-mara-mara-mara-śūṭe-pura svāhā*. Recite the names of the Seven Buddhas together with the names of the Twelve Divine Generals.
Recite this mantra and tie it behind the elbow.
Once the illness has been cured, place it in a pure location, and so forth.
This is the Tathāgata named Śrīvijayaśrīrāja.
The Tathāgata Ratnacandraprajñāvyūhaghoṣeśvararāja;
the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇaratnābhikṣetrasiddhacaryā;
the Tathāgata Aśoka-vara-śrīrājendra.
Copied by Kenjaku on the seventh day of the third month in the third year of Kangwa. Dharmasāgaravarajñānavikrīḍitābhijña Tathāgata and Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha Tathāgata.
